# Studio page fixtures

Three YouTube Studio pages from Nick's own signed-in Studio (creator-analytics#91), for the extension's "Studio page in, figures out" tests. Each file is the page as Chrome drew it (`document.documentElement.outerHTML`), not the HTML Studio first sends, which holds none of the cards. The first line of each file records its Studio URL and save time.

| File | Studio page | Saved |
|---|---|---|
| `dashboard.html` | The dashboard, with the latest video card | 2026-10-10 |
| `content-list.html` | The Content list, Videos tab, first page | 2026-10-10 |
| `video-analytics.html` | One video's analytics page, Overview tab, period "Last 90 days" | 2026-10-10 |

**The analytics period is in the URL.** Studio carries the selected period as the last path segment: `/video/<video id>/analytics/tab-overview/period-quarter` is "Last 90 days". The page's period menu names each period with a `test-id` that matches the segment (the explore links carry the same name as `time_period=quarter`): `week` "Last 7 days", `4_weeks` "Last 28 days", `quarter` "Last 90 days", `year` "Last 365 days", `lifetime` "Since uploaded (lifetime)", and `since_publish`, `first_24_hours`, `current_year`, `minus_1_year`, `current_month`, `minus_1_month`, `minus_2_month` and `fixed`, which the extension does not map. Only `period-quarter` was seen in a URL; #99 confirms the rest in real Studio. The nav drawer's link to the page carries `period-default`.

**What was removed.** Every `script`, `noscript`, `style`, `iframe`, `link` and `meta` element except the charset, so no session token or Studio configuration is in the repo, and every inline event handler. On the dashboard, the Comments card and the Recent activity card, which name other people. The player's playback address on the analytics page, which carried the IP address and a signed session for the video stream, the signatures on the channel's own thumbnail addresses (`sqp` and `rs` on `i9.ytimg.com`), and the affiliate id in a sponsored video's description. Without styles, a fixture opens in a browser as unstyled text, which still shows each surface.

**What was swapped for sample data** (creator-analytics#942, before the repository went public). Every revenue figure: each Content list row's "Est. revenue", the dashboard's "Estimated revenue" and the analytics page's revenue are made-up amounts, in Studio's own format. On the Content list, the scheduled row and the unlisted row carry sample ids (`sampleSched`, `sampleUnlst`) and sample titles, and the scheduled row a sample description. Every figure only the channel owner sees is a made-up value too: on the dashboard, the 28-day subscriber gain, views and watch time with their typical-range tooltips, the 48-hour top videos' views, and the latest video card's click-through rate, average view duration and the ranking tooltip's views (the ranking stays 6 of 10); on the analytics page, the 90-day views and watch time, the views chart's axis, the retention figures, and the 48-hour views and their traffic shares. The analytics page's `mini-card` attribute, which held the 48-hour views by hour and by traffic source as JSON, is removed. The charts' drawn lines keep their saved shapes. Apart from that attribute, the markup is unchanged, so every parser reads the pages as before. The public videos keep their real ids, titles, view counts and the channel's subscriber count, which anyone can read on the channel.

**Studio's stylesheet, for the store screenshots.** `studio.css` is Studio's own stylesheet from the same three saves, cut to the rules these pages use, so the store screenshots (creator-analytics#100) draw them as Studio does. It is YouTube's own file, so it is not committed (creator-analytics#942): `.gitignore` names it, and each machine that takes the screenshots writes its own copy. The full saves stay out of the repository too, since their scripts hold the signed-in session. `apps/extension/test/screenshot/extract-studio-styles.ts` writes it from them, and leaves out a style another extension in that browser had written into the page (`ytsd-style`, which hid Studio's Likes column and trend arrows). Write it again whenever these pages are saved again. No test in the suite reads it; without it, `pnpm --filter @creator-analytics/extension screenshots` stops and says how to write it.
